class_guess: Shift-overflow counter (SOC_2_5_v1 TM10 with A1 = 0RF); halting hinges on the bits of a counter value: cryptid-like
summary: TM10's two binary counters; it can halt only if a counter value x ever has every 1-bit at an odd position
mechanism: SOC_2_5_v1.v TM10's macro rules (A1 = 0LB there, 0RF here): a left counter LC (digits 11/10) counts down, a right counter RC (digits 10000/00000) counts up, and overflows shift digits between them. Every TM10 lemma except ROv3_0/ROv3_1 compiles for this string.

From blank (cfgL(3,6,1) at step 35) every cycle is LOv at cfgL(L,0,2x+1), RC1_Ov_0, c >= 0 RC4_Ov_1, RC4_Ov_0. The chain eats x's 1-bits from the bottom and stops at the first one at an even position, which gives an explicit map (L,x) -> (L',x'). All 20,000 cycles computed (L to 172,193) are like this. The history table has one row per cycle (step column = cycle t).

If every 1-bit of x is at an odd position, the chain empties and the run leaves TM10's cycle into ROv3, where A reads 1. With 0RF that can halt (cfgL(8,0,17) halts at step 10,189,718). Even-position 1-bits grow ~0.36 per cycle (min 7 at cycle 13); chain lengths look random. No invariant is known, so ground rule 6 applies.

template.note: Every TM10 lemma except ROv3_0/ROv3_1 compiles with this string (the scout's Iter.v, which admits those two). They are false here, not just unproved: TM10's invariant P contains halting configurations of this machine (cfgL(8,0,17) halts at step 10,189,718). A proof needs P plus an orbit-specific digit condition (the chain never empties), and that condition is the open part. No other upstream file proves this table from any start.

strategy: No non-halting proof is known. Rule 6: formalize the reduction (Rocq: 'no cycle empties the chain -> ~halts tm c0', from TM10's lemmas and F), then park unless a digit invariant turns up.
risks: Non-halting depends on the binary digits of an exponentially growing orbit (all 1-bits at odd positions must never happen): cryptid-like.
The scout's Iter.v 'nonhalt' admits ROv3_0/ROv3_1, which are false for this machine; it is not evidence.
After an exhaustion the dynamics are unmodelled; halting is shown only from constructed starts, not from blank.

checkpoint_questions.text: Counter value x: every row should contain orange (a 1-bit at an even position). A row with no orange is what halting needs. Does every row show orange?
Halt run: from TM10's ROv3 situation, A reads a 1 (row 3) and heads right instead of left; F reads a 1 at step 91. Do you see the A1 = 0RF difference doing this?
Priority call: halting hinges on the digits of x (cryptid-like, ground rule 6). Should we park it now, or fund one 2 h stage to formalize the reduction in Rocq and search for a digit invariant?

stats.growth: exponential (two binary counters); A reads 1 only at step 10 through 3e10 steps; abstract orbit checked for 20,000 cycles (L to 172,193)

status_reason: Mechanism understood (TM10's macro rules, validated); non-halting needs the orbit of an explicit digit map never to put every 1-bit of x at an odd position. Heuristically never; no invariant known.
